Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaCore Foods Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Thompson, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaCore Foods' third quarter fiscal 2024 results. With me on the call are Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; Mike Rivera, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. VitaCore Foods delivered a solid third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover seven key aspects: new product launches and innovation pipeline update; gross margin percentage; price elasticity observations; decomposition of organic sales growth into volume, price, and mix; A&P, or advertising and promotion, spend and ROI; gross margin guidance and key assumptions; and promotional strategy and effectiveness.

I will now turn the call over to John Ramirez to provide more detail on our financial results.

John Ramirez:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $1.45 billion, representing a 5.2% increase compared to the prior year on an organic basis. Gross margin was 46.2%, driven by pricing actions, supply chain efficiencies, and favorable mix shift. Operating income was $285 million, up 12% year-over-year. Diluted earnings per share were $0.98, reflecting 15% growth. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me start by diving into the decomposition of our Q3 fiscal 2024 organic sales growth, which came in at a robust 5.2%, marking our sixth consecutive quarter of positive organic growth and outperforming the broader CPG industry average of around 2-3%, as tracked by NielsenIQ and IRI data. This performance underscores the strength of our Everyday Essentials portfolio and our ability to navigate a dynamic macroeconomic environment characterized by persistent inflation, shifting consumer behaviors toward value and premiumization, and uneven regional recovery post-pandemic.

Organic sales growth excludes the impacts of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange. We decompose this into volume, price, and mix. Overall: volume +2.1%, price +2.5%, mix +0.6%, totaling 5.2% organic growth.

Volume growth of +2.1% was the standout, with broad-based market share gains. In Personal Care, 35% of sales, volume grew 3.2%, fueled by our Clean Glow skincare line, launching in 15 new SKUs with microbiome-friendly formulations, driving a 1.2-point market share increase in North American mass channels per IRI. Household Essentials, 28% of sales, saw +2.4% volume led by Ultra-Concentrate laundry pods, gaining 80 basis points of ACV through targeted trade promotions. Food & Snacks, 25% of sales, delivered +1.5% despite softer trends, thanks to Better-for-You salty snacks with 12% household penetration growth.

Emerging Markets, 45% of sales, led volume at +3.8% via Project Velocity partnering with 50,000+ kirana stores and WhatsApp delivery, boosting rural penetration 15%. North America contributed +1.9%, Developed Europe +0.5%.

Pricing of +2.5% reflected disciplined actions as input inflation moderated to 4.1% YoY. Modest 3-4% list increases on 70% of portfolio, with elasticity at -2.1, better than industry -2.5. Beauty & Personal Care +3.1%, Food & Snacks +2.8% passing 60% of cocoa inflation. EMKTs +4.2% with tiered pricing, NA +1.8% EDLP, Europe +1.2%.

Mix shift +0.6% from premiumization, premium products now 42% of sales. Household super-premium cleaners +1.1 points in Snacks BFY items.

Looking ahead, Q4 organic 4.5-6.0%, volume +2.5%, pricing +2.0%, mix +0.5%.

Now, turning to our gross margin performance, which came in at 46.2% for the quarter—up 140 basis points year-over-year and 70 basis points sequentially from Q2. This marks our strongest quarterly gross margin in over three years and puts us ahead of our long-term target of 45-47%, comparing favorably to peers like Procter & Gamble at 50.1% and Unilever at 44.8%.

Pricing actions contributed 380 basis points. In North America, 55% of revenue, mid-single-digit increases across FreshClean laundry pods and SnackJoy bars without volume erosion. Europe low-single-digits added 200 basis points.

Supply chain efficiencies added 120 basis points via Factory 4.0 AI predictive maintenance and robotic palletizing, reducing downtime 18% and costs 4%. Commodities like cocoa and palm oil down 12% and 8% helped.

Mix shift +60 basis points from premiumization, HealthBoost beverages at 52% margin vs. 42% standard. E-commerce 22% of sales.

Headwinds: input inflation dairy +6%, PET +9%, freight +5%, FX -20 bps.

Regionally: NA 48.5% up 180 bps, Europe 43.2% down 10 bps, EM 44.8% up 100 bps.

For sustained expansion: precision pricing analytics, sustainable sourcing 95% RSPO palm oil, portfolio optimization divesting low-margin SKUs.

Q4 gross margins 46.5-47.0%.

Before moving to segments, a few minutes on our price elasticity observations from Q3, key to our pricing strategy amid inflation. Overall own-price elasticity -1.6, improved from -2.1 last year and better than five-year average -1.9 or industry -2.2 per NielsenIQ. This supported 4.2% organic growth despite 2.8% inflation, NMV share +110 bps to 14.8%.

By category: Beauty & Personal Care -1.2, FreshGlow premium hair care 5% ASP hike -2.7% volume vs. category -4.1%. Household -1.7, concentrated liquids -1.1. Health & Wellness -1.5, VitaBoost -0.9.

Regionally: NA -1.4, EMEA -1.9, LATAM -2.1, APAC -1.3.

Elasticity Prediction Engine with 92% accuracy enabled 250+ tests. Framework: inelastic heroes 55% sales, precision pricing, shopper apps lowering elasticity 0.4 points.

This resilience positions us for margin expansion to 22%+ FY25.

Finally on financials, our gross margin outlook remains a cornerstone. Q3 45.2% adjusted 45.6%, on track full-year. Guiding FY24 adjusted 46.0-46.5%, Q4 46.3-46.8%.

Pricing +150 bps, 2.5-3% net. Raw materials/freight +100 bps, basket flat to -2% YoY, 70% hedged. Productivity/mix +120 bps, $120M YTD savings from Smart Factory 2.0. FX neutral.

Regional: NA 49%, EMEA 43.5%, APAC/LATAM 47%.

Risks: cocoa +$200/MT -20 bps, 1% elasticity miss -30 bps. This funds capex, R&D.

Following my remarks, Lisa will provide an update on our marketing and brand performance.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, John. We continue to see strong performance across our key brands. Our marketing investments are driving increased consumer engagement, and we are particularly pleased with the results of our recent VitaFuel campaign.

As we dive into our marketing investments, here's a detailed update on our A&P spend, a cornerstone of growth. For FY24 to date, we've deployed $1.25 billion in A&P, about 12% of net sales, in line with peers like P&G and Mondelez at 10-14%. This is a 4% YoY increase versus 7% top-line, via zero-based budgeting.

Consumer advertising 42% or $525M up 8% YoY, digital heavy. Trade promotion 58% $725M flat, promo depth 18% off-shelf.

ROMI 2.6x overall, +15% YoY vs. industry 2.1x. Digital 4.2x, Zest Energy relaunch 5.1x. TV 1.8x.

NA 2.8x, Europe 2.2x, EM 3.4x India standout.

AI MMM with Black Swan shaved 10-15% waste, shopper personalization +25% uplift.

FY24 guide $1.3B or 11.5% sales, 60% digital/RMNs.

On promotional strategy and effectiveness, in Q3 we allocated 18.2% of gross revenue—$1.2 billion—to trade promotion, up from 17.5%. Value-First Acceleration targets 4x+ ROI; Q3 4.3x, +15% YoY.

Sales lift 17% blended. Snacks CrunchTime 22% lift, 1.2 share points. Brick-mortar 85% ACV 2.5x basket uplift. E-comm 28% lift.

NA 4.8x, Europe 3.9x, APAC 5.2x.

PromoAI 92% accuracy cut ineffective promos 22%. Loyalty app 15M users, 28% redemption.

Q4 18.5%, 4.5x ROI, omnichannel Total Store media.

After Lisa, Mike will discuss our supply chain initiatives.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, Lisa. Our focus remains on optimizing our supply chain to enhance efficiency and resilience. We are implementing advanced analytics to improve forecasting and inventory management, which contributed to the $120 million in productivity savings John highlighted. Nearshoring has mitigated freight pressures, and our sustainable sourcing covers 95% RSPO-certified palm oil, reducing costs while aligning with consumer demands for eco-friendly practices. We're also advancing packaging waste reduction efforts, targeting compostable materials across key lines.

Finally, Elena will share insights on our innovation pipeline.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the progress we are making on our new product development initiatives. Our pipeline is robust, and we are confident that our innovations will drive future growth. Our recent product, VitaFuel Protein Bar, is showing promising early results with significant market impact.

Moving now to our new product launches and innovation pipeline update, which continues to be a key growth driver for VitaCore Foods. In the CPG space, innovation is about delivering category-defining products aligning with health, sustainability, and convenience. We've seen robust performance from recent launches, pipeline deep, outpacing category amid macro challenges.

Q3 highlights: three major NPIs in snacks, beverages, proteins. VitaFuel Protein Bar, high-protein low-sugar with upcycled pea protein and ashwagandha, launched 4,500 doors late Q2, $45 million retail sales first full quarter, +28% vs. forecast. Velocity 45% above category, trial 32% IRI, 85% ACV US, Walmart/Target rollout outselling Clif/RXBAR 15-20%.

HydraPure+ electrolyte beverage in Europe/APAC, zero-cal natural, 65% ACV Tesco/Rewe, €22M YTD, repeat 28% vs. 18% benchmark. APAC +15% YoY.

NA 72% NPI sales, premiumization. LATAM VitaNuts $18M, +3 share points. Europe +22% YoY.

Pipeline 25 new SKUs FY24, R&D +14% to $185M, 3.2% sales.

Short-term: Precision-fermented dairy alternatives with Perfect Day, 40% better taste, Q1 2024 2,000 doors. Sustainable snack pods AuraPods mycelium compostable, 50 units/store/week proj.

Mid-term: AI CoreLab cut cycles 18 to 9 months, low-glycemic baked goods, upcycled bars.

Pillars: health <5g sugar 80% pipeline, circular 100% recyclable/compostable 2025, e-comm 40% trial 2x repeat.

12-15% NPI to top-line FY24 vs. industry 8%. Risks cocoa/nuts +20%, hedged 70%.

Scale will drive margin expansion.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. The floor is now open for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan.

Sarah Lee:
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce packaging waste and the associated cost savings?

Mike Rivera:
Thanks for the question, Sarah. Reducing packaging waste is a top priority in our supply chain strategy, directly tying into the sustainability initiatives supporting our innovation and margin performance. We've made strong progress this year, aligning with the three pillars Elena outlined—particularly circular economy goals. For instance, our AuraPods sustainable snack pods use mycelium-based compostable materials from partners like Ecovative, addressing the 68% of consumers prioritizing eco-packaging per NielsenIQ. This has rolled out in pilot to 1,200 stores, reducing plastic waste by 45% per unit while maintaining velocity at 50 units per store per week.

Cost savings have been meaningful: across our broader portfolio, we've cut packaging costs by 8% or $32 million YTD through lighter materials and right-sizing, without impacting shelf appeal. This contributed 20 basis points to gross margin expansion, as John noted, via avoided EU deforestation tariffs and supplier premiums for recycled content. In Europe, where regs are toughest, our 100% recyclable goal by 2025 has already saved €15 million in compliance avoidance.

We're scaling with precision-fermented packaging trials and blockchain tracking for transparency, boosting willingness-to-pay by 10-15%. Risks like raw material volatility are hedged, but this positions us ahead of peers like Unilever. Happy to follow up offline.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Goldman Sachs.

David Kim:
How are you leveraging data analytics to personalize your marketing efforts and improve customer engagement?

Lisa Patel:
Great question, David. Data analytics is at the heart of our personalization strategy, fueling the ROMI and promo effectiveness John and I discussed. We're using our Elasticity Prediction Engine and PromoAI platform—ML models on 5+ years IRI/Nielsen POS data plus first-party panels—to deliver hyper-personalized experiences at SKU-store-week level, 92% accuracy.

In marketing, this powers shopper-centric initiatives like our Rewards app with 15 million MAUs, pushing personalized offers via geofencing and zero-party data exchanges with Amazon. For Q3, 65% beverage lift from app-exclusive B2G1 50% off, redemption 28% vs. industry 12%. E-comm personalization drove 28% lift, repeat +35%, AOV $48.

On engagement, programmatic/CTV for Zest Energy yielded 5.1x ROMI, 28% penetration lift 18-34 demo. Retail media like Walmart Connect/Target Roundel 5x+ ROI, precision targeting.

In APAC, Tmall pilots -0.8 elasticity China. This lowers effective elasticity 0.4 points, locks loyalty. FY24 expanding gen-AI creatives, targeting 20% ROMI boost DTC 8% sales. Outperforming peers via data flywheel.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Rodriguez:
What is the expected impact of recent commodity price increases on your gross margins?

John Ramirez:
Thanks, Emily. Commodity volatility is always top of mind, and we've embedded conservative assumptions in our guidance as I outlined. Recent increases—cocoa up post-West Africa weather, palm oil spot $1,050/MT—have pressured inputs, but our hedging covers 70% of 2024 needs, capping cocoa at +5% exposure. Reformulations reduced cocoa 10% in snacks without taste compromise, like Hershey's playbook.

In Q3, favorable YoY cocoa/palm declines lifted 120 bps, but Q4 assumes flat to -2% basket despite spikes. Sensitivity: +$200/MT cocoa = -20 bps hit, offset by productivity $200M FY24. Pricing 2.5-3% and mix pass-through mitigate.

Regionally, EMKTs hedged local, NA e-comm efficiencies. No Black Sea/Red Sea escalation assumed. Overall, FY24 guide 46.0-46.5% holds, with 100 bps+ expansion via levers. Prepared for upside deflation too.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Wilson with Bank of America.

Tom Wilson:
Can you discuss the competitive landscape and any emerging trends that are impacting your market share?

Sarah Chen:
Sure, Tom. The CPG landscape remains competitive with private label aggression from Aldi/Lidl/Walmart Kirkland, inflation-driven downtrading, and premiumization. But our execution—5.2% organic growth vs. industry 2-3%—drove share gains: NMV +110 bps to 14.8%, 1.2 points skincare, 80 bps ACV laundry, salty snacks vs. Frito-Lay/Mondelez.

Trends: functional wellness post-pandemic, sustainability (68% priority), e-comm 22% sales. Our NPIs like VitaFuel +28% forecast, outselling Clif/RXBAR 15-20%, HydraPure 28% repeat. Elasticity -1.6 better than P&G/Unilever.

Health adjacency 80% pipeline <5g sugar, circular packaging. Digital personalization loyalty apps 12M users. EMKTs velocity kirana/Whatsapp +15% pen.

Outpacing peers: vs. Colgate flat volumes, Reckitt declining. Risks tariffs/private labels, but 11 quarters share stability, ROIC +4.2%. Confident strategy wins.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your thoughtful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to updating you next quarter.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the VitaCore Foods Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
